edits.new: Establish the broadest coherent explicit meaning supported by the evidence for the selected entry in a social-media post.
edits.old: Establish the explicit meaning of the selected entry in a social-media post.

edits.new: Distinguish a complete set expressly defined by the selected subject from descendants illustrating members of a broader category.
edits.old: Also consider whether supplied descendants illustrate a broader category or establish its full membership.

edits.new:
Choose the broadest coherent meaning of the selected topic supported by its subject in the sense established by its context, original hierarchy and post. Breadth concerns what information belongs under that same topic. The evidence need not illustrate every member of a broader category; the category's scope must follow from the selected subject in its intended sense.

Preserve the subject's expressed restrictions and named identity, including all explicitly named alternatives and parts. Use ancestors and descendants to interpret its sense and level of abstraction. Their example-specific details do not automatically restrict the selected topic. Preserve the distinction between several parts required together and alternatives admitted independently, with each alternative's own expressed restrictions. Do not discard a named part or add a restriction to fit an inferred parent meaning. If the selected subject identifies a particular person, thing or collection, retain that identity.

For competing broader and narrower interpretations of the same topic, retain an additional restriction only when the selected subject expresses it or the defining features of its intended sense require it. When both interpretations are supported and one includes the other, choose the broader one. When interpretations concern different senses or identities, resolve that difference from the input; do not combine them to manufacture a larger category. Unknown facts about an instance remain unknown even when a broader category is chosen.

For an activity, choose a concrete condition stating its defining action or process. Decide which actions are required and which methods are optional, retaining any required purpose or product alongside the action. If competing process conditions admit different activities, record and resolve that boundary; naming the activity or listing possible methods does not settle it. For a particular instance, retain the chosen process while preserving uncertainty about unmentioned methods, tools and outcomes.

The choices must form one coherent meaning. In each `resolutions.answer`, state the chosen membership condition: the properties, role, purpose or state that qualify information for the topic. Specify whether a condition characterizes a kind or must hold for a particular instance. In `justification`, briefly explain each retained restriction and why the chosen scope is the broadest supported interpretation. Repeating the selected subject is not enough to settle membership. If the evidence cannot establish one coherent meaning, use a null answer for the unresolved ambiguity.
edits.old:
Resolve each ambiguity using the selected subject, its context, the original branch and the post. Preserve the subject's expressed restrictions and named identity, including all explicitly named alternatives and parts. Use ancestors and descendants to help interpret its sense and level of abstraction. A relationship cannot add a restriction missing from the selected subject or justify discarding part of it to make it fit. A description requiring several parts together may narrow the topic of a required part; the other parts need not be instances of that part's kind or action. Decide whether multiple named parts must be described together or are alternatives admitted independently. Co-mention alone does not settle this. Preserve the restrictions the selected subject applies to each admitted alternative. If a coherent interpretation of the selected subject cannot be justified, record the ambiguity as unresolved.

For an activity, choose a concrete condition stating its defining action or process. Decide which actions are required and which methods are optional, retaining any required purpose or product alongside the action. If competing process conditions admit different activities, record and resolve that boundary; naming the activity or listing possible methods does not settle it. For a particular instance, retain the chosen process while preserving uncertainty about unmentioned methods, tools and outcomes.

When the selected subject admits competing senses or defining boundaries, make a justified choice that preserves its level of abstraction and expressed restrictions. Do not substitute a broader or narrower topic or combine competing interpretations to avoid deciding. The choices must fit together as one coherent meaning. In each `resolutions.answer`, state the concrete membership condition chosen for that ambiguity: the properties, role, purpose or state that qualify something for the category. Specify whether the condition characterizes the kind or must hold for the particular example. Repeating the selected subject is not enough to resolve a difference in membership. Put the brief justification and explanations of rejected interpretations in `justification`; use a null answer if no coherent condition can be justified.
